stop_snooping emits the exact active/inactive messages and clears the bidirectional descriptor link (R1/R4/R5e).
C emits No such person around with its CRLF, rather than an invented online-only response (R1/R5e).
Visible NPC lookup reaches the descriptor-less target branch and emits C's no-link bytes (R1/R3/R5e).

Victim output is forwarded to the snooper with C's percent delimiters; this is a descriptor-level re-entrant path (R1/R3/R5e).
A repeat request sees victim->desc->snoop_by and returns Busy already without toggling state (R1/R4/R5e).

Naming the snooper itself reaches stop_snooping, not a toggle-on-self invention (R1/R4/R5e).
C rejects a target at or above the snooper's level with You can't, including the exact equality boundary (R1/R2/R5e).
A target already linked to another snooper remains busy and cannot be stolen (R1/R4/R5e).
The dispatcher passes the first argument token; trailing words do not alter target resolution (R2/R3/R5e).
Descriptor input is relayed before command routing with C's percent prefix and CRLF (R1/R3/R5e).
The reciprocal snooping link is rejected with Don't be stupid before level comparison (R1/R4/R5e).
A descriptor's switched original is the level-comparison target, matching the C original-pointer branch (R1/R5e).
